text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementPaleontology“Astonishing” Find: Fossilized Dinosaur Blood in a 115-Million-Year-Old SpecimenMolecular paleontology keeps getting betterJCBy Jake Currie1:00 PM CST on November 6, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleDinosaur blood may have built the fictional Jurassic Park, but coming across it in the real world has proved to be a little more difficult—until now. In a new study published in Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, a team of paleontologists and geochemists announced they’ve struck 115-million-year-old paydirt.  Powered By 10 ShareNextStayThe team found the blood cells in the hind leg bone of a juvenile Cretaceous-era theropod (Aratasaurus museunacionali) excavated from a Brazilian mine in 2008. After taking thin slices of the fossilized bones, chemically treating them, and giving them a thorough inspection under an electron microscope, they discovered round blobs roughly the size of cells.
